messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE to #incidents — GPU pool 'worker-gpu-prod' queued requests >95% for 6m, mean queue depth 420, p50 latency 1.8s -> 6s. HPA for deployment 'inference-gpu' not scaling (metrics-server adapter returning 503s).

mike_oncall: I'm on it. linking the alert: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/2139998887

jen_sre: I'm seeing the same in grafana — prometheus scrape for 'gpu_utilization' dropped to stale around 2139995200. adapter logs show `Error: upstream read timeout`.

tom_ml: customer-facing impact? any 5xx/429 spike?

ana_support: Support queue has multiple tickets showing timeouts from customers using hosted inference. A few large customers reported increased response times and some 429s. I've flagged 2 enterprise customers for CS to handle.

mike_oncall: ok priority = P1. Plan: 1) mitigate customer impact (scale up manually & route traffic) 2) fix metrics pipeline (metrics-adapter restart) 3) restore autoscale and rollback manual changes.

lucy_runtime: If HPA isn't seeing metrics we can temporarily scale the inference deployment and block new non-dedicated traffic. I'll prepare commands.

bryan_ops: also seeing API gateway throttles engaged — gateway rate limiter bumped to protect control plane, which may explain 429s. I'll reduce burst to allow steady traffic to dedicated pools.

mike_oncall: perform manual scale to relieve queue.

lucy_runtime: running:
```bash
kubectl -n production scale deploy inference-gpu --replicas=20
kubectl -n production rollout status deploy/inference-gpu
```

lucy_runtime: done — replicas increased from 6 -> 20, rollout succeeded. queue depth dropping now (p95 queue depth 120).

jen_sre: restarting metrics adapter pod to clear upstream timeout cache.

jen_sre: command:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/prometheus-metrics-adapter
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/prometheus-metrics-adapter -f --tail=200
```

jen_sre: adapter logs after restart show initial errors but then successful scrapes to prometheus: `200 OK`. Metrics latency back to normal.

tom_ml: good — HPA should pick up metrics, what's HPA status?

lucy_runtime: checking:
```bash
kubectl -n production get hpa inference-gpu -o yaml
# shows currentReplicas: 20, desiredReplicas: 40 (based on new metrics), maxReplicas: 50
```

mike_oncall: HPA now reporting desired 40 but cluster resource quotas will limit further scale. Are we hitting node pool limits?

bryan_ops: yes, GKE autoscaler has a scaling cooldown and we hit GPU quota for the region. I'm requesting capacity bump but that's not immediate. Short term we can spill to dedicated capacity region or reduce per-request concurrency to increase throughput.

ana_support: customers still see degraded latencies but fewer 429s. I posted an update to affected customers.

mike_oncall: handoff incoming — @jen_sre will take over for the next hour, I'm going offline for lunch (30m). Leave channel updates. :thumbsup:

jen_sre: acknowledged, taking lead. Current action items: 1) monitor HPA progress 2) coordinate with ops for capacity 3) follow up on metrics-adapter root cause.

jen_sre: noticed metrics-adapter pod had a spike of `too many open files` errors before the outage. Suspect a leak in the adapter's Prometheus client. I'll open an issue and pin logs.

tom_ml: can we enable a secondary autoscaling fallback? e.g., KEDA scaler on queue length or custom prometheus rule so we don't rely solely on adapter?

lucy_runtime: we have an emergency fallback runbook. Quick patch: apply a KEDA ScaledObject that uses the SQS/redis queue length metric we already export. Doing that now as a temporary measure.

lucy_runtime: applying ScaledObject:
```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: inference-gpu-queue-scaler
  namespace: production
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: inference-gpu
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prometheus.monitoring.svc
      metricName: custom_queue_depth
      threshold: '200'
```

lucy_runtime: KEDA created and scaled additional pods to 32 quickly. queue depth p95 down to 40.

ana_support: sharing status update to customers now: "We've applied mitigations and are seeing traffic normalization; some customers may still experience higher latency while we finish capacity increase."

bryan_ops: cloud quota request submitted to infra (case 987654). ETA ~2 hours. For now dedicated-capacity redirect is live for 3 large tenants.

jen_sre: postmortem action items so far: 1) harden metrics-adapter (file descriptor leak) 2) add fallback KEDA autoscale for critical paths 3) improve runbook for gateway rate limiter interactions 4) add alert for adapter FD exhaustion 5) capacity playbook to spill to dedicated capacity automatically.

mike_oncall: back from lunch, thanks team. Anything outstanding?

lucy_runtime: main outstanding: we still need to revert manual scaling once quota increases or HPA stabilizes, and file RCA for adapter. Also confirm no regression from KEDA patch.

tom_ml: any long-term model-serving changes? We should consider lowering per-request GPU memory target to allow more pods per node and reduce chance of node quota. I'll spin a proposal.

jen_sre: created incident doc and pinned logs: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2139998887. I'll start RCA draft.

ana_support: I'll follow up with the two enterprise contacts and confirm recovery.

bryan_ops: cloud quota approved in 1h earlier than expected, autoscaler is adding nodes now. HPA desired->current will catch up.

jen_sre: metrics-adapter fix: opened GH issue https://github.com/redwood/metrics-adapter/issues/432 and marked P0. Assigning to eng-infra.

mike_oncall: moving this to post-incident review. Great job coordinating. Closing paging run once metrics stable for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident 2139998887 transitioned to RESOLVED (mitigations applied, autoscaling restored)"
